name: Foot and Mouth Disease
firstAid: Isolate affected animals immediately. Restrict movement on and off the farm. Contact your vet and report to animal health authorities. Provide soft feed and clean water. Do not move animals.

name: East Coast Fever
firstAid: Call your vet immediately — this disease kills within 2-4 weeks without treatment. Isolate the animal. Keep it in the shade and provide fresh water. Do not attempt home treatment.

name: Lumpy Skin Disease
firstAid: Isolate affected animals. Contact your vet for antiviral or supportive treatment. Control biting insects with insecticide. Vaccinate the rest of the herd if available.

name: Contagious Caprine Pleuropneumonia (CCPP)
firstAid: Isolate sick animals immediately. Call the vet — antibiotics work if given early. Prevent contact between your goats and any new animals. Report to county livestock office.

name: Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR)
firstAid: Isolate sick animals. Call your vet and report to county livestock office. Provide electrolytes and supportive care. Vaccinate the rest of the herd.

name: Pneumonia
firstAid: Move the animal to a dry sheltered area. Reduce stress. Call your vet for antibiotic treatment. Ensure good ventilation in the housing.

name: Trypanosomiasis (Nagana)
firstAid: Remove animals from areas with tsetse flies. Call your vet for trypanocidal drug treatment. Use insect control measures. Check blood smear to confirm diagnosis.

name: Brucellosis
firstAid: Isolate the animal. Do not consume milk or handle birth materials without gloves — this can infect humans. Call your vet. Report to county health and livestock offices.

name: Newcastle Disease
firstAid: Isolate affected birds immediately. Call your vet and report to county livestock office. Vaccinate all healthy birds if not already done. Improve biosecurity.

name: Fowl Typhoid
firstAid: Isolate sick birds. Call your vet for antibiotic treatment. Improve sanitation and water hygiene. Remove and safely dispose of dead birds.

name: Coccidiosis
firstAid: Provide anticoccidial treatment in water as directed by your vet. Improve litter management and hygiene. Ensure clean dry bedding.

name: Marek's Disease
firstAid: No treatment available. Cull severely affected birds. Vaccinate chicks at hatch. Improve ventilation and reduce crowding.

name: Blackleg
firstAid: This disease kills within 24-48 hours — call your vet immediately. Vaccinate the rest of the herd urgently. Remove and safely bury or burn the carcass away from water sources.

name: Anthrax
firstAid: Do not touch or move the carcass — anthrax can kill humans. Call your vet and county livestock officer immediately. Vaccinate all other animals. This is a notifiable disease.

name: Heartwater
firstAid: Call your vet immediately — early antibiotic treatment can save the animal. Control ticks with approved acaricide. Keep animals away from tick-infested areas.
